memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium (a working hypothesis on the return, high on the business). The case is a good business at a fair price, not a compelling one: on the record's modal path the return is 12.1 percent a year over eighteen months and 9.6 percent a year over three years against the 20 percent bar. The gate does not park it (no D or F on management A, business quality A, predictability C or trackability C); it is parked on price and return. Progress at about SEK 285 (where the eighteen-month path clears the bar), or on evidence that would earn the re-rating the record does not assume: H2 2026 acquisitions of SEK 2.5 billion or more of annualised sales; the Demolition & Tools EBITA margin above 25 percent by Q1 2027; the short-seller report of 14 January 2026 obtained and answered. Invalidate on any restatement, impairment or auditor qualification, or on two consecutive half-years below SEK 1 billion of annualised acquired sales.
case: Lifco is a twenty-year compounder whose ordinary compounding was interrupted by a 2025 industrial trough and by a short-seller report nobody in the research chain has read, and at SEK 317.8 the shares have already paid for the part of the resumption the record can see.

The change is external and cyclical, and ordinary for this company. The industrial half had its worst year since the 2014 listing in 2025 (organic EBITA growth 0.1 percent; Demolition & Tools organic sales -9.2 percent). The Q2 2026 report of 14 July 2026 showed the turn: organic growth 4.7 percent against 3.4 percent consensus, after 1.2 percent in Q1 2026 and -2.0 percent in Q2 2025; Contract Manufacturing +16.1 percent; Environmental Technology +10.3 percent to SEK 886 million; Transportation Products +22.0 percent to SEK 1,100 million; Dental +4.9 percent to SEK 1,678 million. Management calls 2025 the trough and H1 2026 "a clear return to normality"; the comparatives were easy. Two external headwinds run against the turn: SEK strength (FX took 3 percent off H1 2026 sales, 4.7 percent off Q1 2026 EBITA, 3.1 percent off 2025 EBITA; 83 percent of EBITA is earned outside Sweden; a 10 percent SEK move against the euro is SEK 210 million of pre-tax profit; Nordea has EUR/SEK at 10.40 by end-2027) and a construction cycle that has not turned for demolition robots (Eurozone construction PMI 42.8 in June 2026; the Demolition & Tools six-month margin -130 basis points to 23.9 percent; segment sales +1.8 percent in Q2 2026 to SEK 1,806 million). Rates are a fourth headwind, on the multiple (STIBOR about 2.0 percent against 0 percent in 2022). 'Macroeconomic' is rated D because the translation exposure is larger at Lifco than at Addtech, Lagercrantz or Beijer Alma. The company's own cycle is rated B: it has turned, but one quarter off easy comparatives is the evidence.

Nothing inside the company has changed, and that is the strength of the business and the weakness of the thesis as a change story. Per Waldemarson has been chief executive since 2019, with the group since 2006; the strategy is explicitly unchanged ("never sells a business"); the company gives no numerical guidance at all ("We don't forecast the future in Lifco"), so 'Guidance raised' is D and 'Perimeter reduction' is D by policy. The acquisition programme is disciplined (5.8x to 6.8x pro-forma EBITA from 2012 to 2024; acquired margins about 29 percent) but ran slower in H1 2026: four acquisitions, about SEK 500 million of annualised sales, SEK 1,186 million of cash in the first two periods of FY2026 against SEK 3,361 million in FY2025; Redeye says "a faster M&A pace is ideally required". The one internal step, five segments from three, is a capacity choice to source more deals. Pricing is real and applied (3 to 7 percent in the first year after a deal; 3 to 6 percent a year in the niches; 10 percent in dental software; the Q2 2026 margin against DNB Carnegie's expectation of a flat one) but a standing practice, rated B not A. Interest-bearing net debt at 1.2x sits below the company's own 2.0x to 3.0x range; the room is a strength of the foundations, not a change force. The dividend rose 12.5 percent to SEK 2.70 (consensus SEK 2.90, 3.30, 3.60); no buybacks, none mooted. The one other internal development is defensive: the short-seller report of 14 January 2026 has not been obtained or rebutted (DNB Carnegie could not access it); the answer has been delivery.
counter_case: At its strongest, from the risks report's "false friend" verdict and the sceptics in the earnings review: Lifco's reported compounding is an acquisition-driven headline that masks flat organic earnings, and the ten-year-median multiple is not fair but generous. Organic EBITA growth was 0.1 percent in 2025 and Dental's organic EBITA grows 1 percent a year through a cycle; the decade's growth was two-thirds acquired. Margins are held by low-margin onward invoicing and by adding back about SEK 1.1 billion a year of acquired-intangible amortisation to reach EBITA; SEK 3,060 million of put/call liabilities for future minority buy-outs sit off the headline; there is no internal audit function over 275 companies, by board decision; 16 whistleblower cases in 2025 against 11. A three-person centre is already the bottleneck: H1 2026 deals ran at a quarter of the 2025 pace, the Head of Acquisitions who left in 2022 was not replaced, former acquisition executives say the valuation filter restricts deployment, and the acquisition market is turning against the model as private equity, search funds and rival serial acquirers bid up the same SEK 100 to 150 million niche targets. The model's premium multiple was built on cheap money (STIBOR at 0 percent in 2022 against about 2.0 percent now; the multiple at 41.55x five years ago) and a fragmented acquisition market, and both have gone. 83 percent of EBITA is earned outside Sweden and the sell-side's FX houses expect EUR/SEK at 10.40 by end-2027, a 2 to 3 percent annual earnings drag. The short-seller report of 14 January 2026 has not been rebutted because, on this reading, it cannot be; the company's silence for eight months is a choice, and the report's known targets (the accounting; the sustainability of the decentralised model) are permanent features, not transient concerns. On that reading the right 'Target Setup' is none of the six, the nearest is a false 'Compounder' (heavy coverage, a correctly modelled business, a C at best), the trough multiple is 18.6x to 22.7x, the downside is 15 to 31 percent with earnings unchanged and 30 to 55 percent in the bear models (DNB Carnegie's SEK 270 bear case; Redeye's SEK 136 to 180), and six Ds around a thesis whose only A is the operator (broad mediocrity, modal return, multiple risk, perimeter, the market leg of congruence, earnings momentum and valuation pinned) make a case to invalidate, not to watch; "park" is too kind for a stock at its ten-year median with an unread short report and a 15 to 31 percent multiple downside.

What the record concedes: the organic engine is slow and cyclical; the amortisation gap and the put/call liabilities are real claims that the adjusted-basis brokers ignore and the record's reported-basis metric does not; the H1 2026 cadence is the case's live weakness; the translation exposure is larger than peers' and the FX houses are against it; the mark-to-market risk at a median multiple is large and is rated D; the oversold condition holds only partly; the sentiment concern cannot be shown transient until the report is answered or expires; the centre is thin at the top and the succession plan is undisclosed; the report is unread and the company's silence is a choice the record would not have made; the Ds are real and none has been softened; the thesis is bland; the return does not clear the bar on any branch the record calls probable.
triggers: - The price trigger: progress at about SEK 285 on the eighteen-month path (SEK 287 by the arithmetic); about SEK 260 on the three-year path with the multiple held (SEK 259) or SEK 242 with the fade.

- M&A deployment pace (Key Driver): monitor annualised acquired sales announced per half-year, the paid multiple on each material deal, the deal count. Current: H1 2026 four acquisitions, about SEK 500 million of annualised sales. Modal: SEK 2.0 to 2.5 billion a year at 6 to 7x EBITA; probable at about 70 percent. Confirm at SEK 2.5 billion or more of annualised acquired sales in H2 2026. Alarm below SEK 1.5 billion in H2 2026. Invalidate on fewer than ten deals in a year or a paid multiple above 8x EBITA on a material deal.

- Industrial organic recovery (Key Driver): quarterly organic growth (current 4.7 percent in Q2 2026; modal 3 to 5 percent through 2027; probable at about 60 percent; alarm below 2 percent in a quarter; invalidate below 1 percent in Dental or Systems Solutions); the Demolition & Tools EBITA margin (current 23.9 percent in H1 2026; modal above 25 percent by Q1 2027; alarm still below 24 percent in Q1 2027); the Eurozone and German construction PMIs (current 42.8 in June 2026; modal above 50 by Q4 2026).

- The multiple (Key Driver): the 24-month-forward P/E (current 26.9x blended, 28.9x on the record's reported basis; modal held at 28.9x reported at eighteen months, 27.0x at three years; plausible at near-even odds that it holds); the gap to Addtech and Lagercrantz; Swedish rates. Alarm 24x blended. Invalidate 22.7x blended, the ten-year 35th percentile. Up-side change of view: the report published and answered; down-side: a peer short attack or a 50-basis-point rise in Swedish rates.

- Short-seller allegations (Key Risk): any restatement, impairment or auditor qualification invalidates; the report obtained (the risks report's single highest due-diligence priority) and management's response would move the view up.

- SEK strength (Key Risk): EUR/SEK; the record's path carries -1.5 percent a year of translation; alarm at EUR/SEK below 10.5 for two quarters, which moves the path to the adverse case and the rating to F; consensus EUR/SEK 10.40 by end-2027.
